Logistic Regression.explanation: Simple linear model used for binary classification with probabilistic output
points: Uses sigmoid function to map linear combination to probability between 0 and 1
Interpretable — coefficients show feature importance and direction of impact
Trained with maximum likelihood estimation and gradient descent
Regularization (L1/L2) prevents overfitting and performs feature selection
Baseline model for most binary classification problems before trying complex models

Decision Tree.explanation: Tree-based model that makes decisions by splitting features based on thresholds
points: Non-parametric — no assumptions about data distribution
Splits chosen to maximize information gain or Gini impurity reduction
Prone to overfitting — needs pruning or depth/max_leaf_nodes limits
Very interpretable — can be visualized as a flowchart
Foundation for ensemble methods like Random Forest and Gradient Boosting

Random Forest.explanation: Ensemble of decision trees using bagging and feature randomness for better accuracy
points: Reduces overfitting compared to single decision tree via averaging predictions
Feature importance score helps understand which variables drive decisions
Handles missing values and mixed data types naturally
Out-of-bag (OOB) error provides internal validation without separate test set
One of the strongest off-the-shelf models for tabular data

Gradient Boosting.explanation: Sequential ensemble technique that builds trees to correct previous errors
points: Optimizes arbitrary differentiable loss functions via gradient descent in function space
XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost are popular high-performance implementations
Strong regularization options (learning rate, subsampling, tree pruning)
Usually outperforms Random Forest on structured/tabular data
Feature importance and partial dependence plots aid interpretability

Support Vector Machine.explanation: Powerful classifier that finds the optimal hyperplane with maximum margin
points: Maximizes margin between classes using support vectors
Kernel trick allows non-linear classification without explicit transformation
Common kernels: linear, RBF (Gaussian), polynomial, sigmoid
Effective in high-dimensional spaces (text classification, bioinformatics)
C parameter controls trade-off between margin and misclassification

Neural Network.explanation: Interconnected nodes organized in layers that learn complex patterns
points: Universal function approximators — can model any continuous function
Trained with backpropagation and gradient descent variants (Adam, RMSprop)
Activation functions (ReLU, GELU, Swish) introduce non-linearity
Deep networks require regularization (dropout, weight decay, batch norm)
Foundation for almost all modern deep learning architectures

Convolutional Neural Network.explanation: Specialized neural network for grid-like data like images using convolution
points: Convolution + pooling layers extract hierarchical spatial features
Parameter sharing and sparse connectivity reduce computation and parameters
Local receptive fields capture translation-invariant patterns
Architectures: LeNet, AlexNet, VGG, ResNet, EfficientNet, ConvNeXt
Dominates computer vision tasks since 2012 ImageNet breakthrough

Recurrent Neural Network.explanation: Neural network designed for sequential data with loops in the architecture
points: Maintains hidden state that captures information from previous timesteps
Vanishing/exploding gradients problem addressed by LSTM and GRU
Used for time series, NLP, speech recognition before transformers
Bidirectional RNNs capture context from both directions
Mostly replaced by transformers in NLP but still used in some time-series tasks

LSTM.explanation: Long Short-Term Memory cell that addresses vanishing gradient problem in RNNs
points: Three gates (forget, input, output) control information flow
Cell state acts as conveyor belt — long-term dependencies preserved
Widely used in speech recognition, machine translation, time series
Peephole connections and coupled input-forget gate are common variants
Still relevant in resource-constrained or sequential modeling tasks

GRU.explanation: Gated Recurrent Unit — simplified LSTM with fewer parameters
points: Two gates (update, reset) instead of three — computationally lighter
Often performs similarly to LSTM with faster training
Popular in mobile/edge devices and real-time applications
Reset gate controls how much past information to forget
Update gate decides how much past information to carry forward

Transformer.explanation: Architecture based entirely on attention mechanisms — no recurrence or convolution
points: Self-attention allows modeling long-range dependencies efficiently
Multi-head attention captures different types of relationships
Positional encoding adds sequence order information
Foundation of nearly all state-of-the-art NLP and vision models since 2017
Scales very well with data and compute (scaling laws)

BERT.explanation: Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers — pre-trained language model
points: Trained with masked language modeling and next sentence prediction
Bidirectional context understanding — major improvement over left-to-right models
Fine-tuning achieves SOTA on most NLP tasks in 2018–2019
Variants: RoBERTa, ALBERT, DistilBERT, ELECTRA, DeBERTa
Still widely used as backbone for many downstream tasks

Vision Transformer.explanation: Transformer architecture applied directly to image patches instead of convolutions
points: Splits image into fixed-size patches → treats as sequence
ViT (2020) showed transformers can outperform CNNs with enough data
Variants: Swin Transformer, DeiT, CaiT, BEiT, MAE
Strong scaling behavior — larger models + more data = better performance
Now dominant in many computer vision benchmarks

YOLO.explanation: You Only Look Once — real-time object detection family of models
points: Single-stage detector — predicts bounding boxes and classes in one pass
YOLOv1 (2015) → YOLOv8/YOLOv10 (2024–2025) — massive speed/accuracy improvements
Anchor-free versions (YOLOv5+, YOLOv8) improved generalization
Widely used in autonomous driving, surveillance, robotics
Balances speed and accuracy better than two-stage detectors

Faster R-CNN.explanation: Two-stage object detection model with Region Proposal Network
points: Region Proposal Network (RPN) generates candidate boxes efficiently
Second stage classifies and refines boxes
Introduced ROI pooling → ROI Align improved accuracy
Mask R-CNN extension adds instance segmentation
Strong baseline for many detection and segmentation tasks

EfficientNet.explanation: Family of CNNs that scale depth, width, and resolution optimally
points: Compound scaling method — balances all dimensions together
EfficientNet-B7 outperformed previous SOTA with 8.4× fewer parameters
EfficientNetV2 improved training speed and regularization
Widely used backbone for classification and detection
Mobile-friendly variants (EfficientNet-Lite)

ResNet.explanation: Residual Network — introduced skip connections to enable very deep CNNs
points: Residual blocks — shortcut connections solve vanishing gradient problem
ResNet-50/101/152 became de-facto backbones after 2015
ResNeXt introduced cardinality (grouped convolutions)
ResNet-D improved stem and downsampling
Still widely used in 2025 due to maturity and speed

MobileNet.explanation: Lightweight CNN architecture optimized for mobile and edge devices
points: Depthwise separable convolutions reduce parameters and computation
MobileNetV3 + h-swish + squeeze-and-excitation → very efficient
Used in on-device vision (face detection, OCR, AR)
Quantization and pruning friendly
Backbone for many edge AI applications

GAN.explanation: Generative Adversarial Network — two networks competing to generate realistic data
points: Generator vs Discriminator minimax game
DCGAN, StyleGAN, BigGAN, StyleGAN3, Diffusion models largely replaced pure GANs
Mode collapse and training instability are classic challenges
Conditional GANs (cGAN) generate specific classes/styles
Still used in image-to-image translation (CycleGAN, Pix2Pix)

Diffusion Model.explanation: Generative model that learns to reverse a noising process to create data
points: State-of-the-art image/video generation in 2025 (Stable Diffusion, DALL·E 3, Imagen 3)
Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPM) foundation
Latent diffusion (LDM) makes training feasible
Classifier-free guidance improves prompt adherence
Fast samplers (DDIM, Heun, LCM, Consistency Models) enable real-time generation

Vision-Language Model.explanation: Models trained jointly on images and text for multimodal understanding
points: CLIP (2021) — contrastive learning on 400M image-text pairs
Flamingo, BLIP, BLIP-2, LLaVA, Kosmos-2, Qwen-VL, InternVL
Enable zero-shot classification, image captioning, visual question answering
Most use frozen vision encoder + LLM with projection layer
Scaling laws apply strongly — bigger models + more data = much better performance

Segment Anything Model.explanation: Foundation model for image segmentation — segments anything with prompts
points: SAM (2023) — trained on 1B+ masks on 11M images
Promptable — point, box, mask, text (with extensions)
Zero-shot generalization to unseen objects/domains
SAM 2 (2024) extends to video segmentation
Ecosystem: MobileSAM, FastSAM, Grounding DINO + SAM
Combines YOLO architecture with CLIP-style text encoder
Detects arbitrary objects given text prompt (zero-shot)
Very fast inference — real-time on edge devices
Popular for robotics, autonomous driving, video surveillance
Easily fine-tuned on custom classes

U-Net.explanation: Classic architecture for biomedical image segmentation with encoder-decoder structure
points: Symmetric encoder-decoder with skip connections
Still widely used in medical imaging and diffusion models
Attention U-Net, UNet++, TransUNet, Swin-UNet are modern variants
Very effective with limited labeled data
Backbone of many segmentation pipelines

Mask R-CNN.explanation: Extension of Faster R-CNN that adds instance segmentation branch
points: Detects objects + generates pixel-level masks
ROI Align instead of ROI Pooling improves mask accuracy
Used in COCO dataset and many real-world applications
Detectron2 and MMDetection provide strong implementations
Foundation for many modern segmentation models

Swin Transformer.explanation: Hierarchical vision transformer with shifted windows for efficient computation
points: Shifted window attention reduces complexity from quadratic to linear
Hierarchical feature maps — works well with detection/segmentation
SOTA performance on ImageNet and COCO in 2021–2022
Swin V2 improved stability and scaling
Widely used backbone in 2025

ConvNeXt.explanation: Modernized CNN that competes with transformers using updated design choices
points: Modernized ResNet with transformer-inspired improvements
Large kernel sizes, layer normalization, patchify stem
ConvNeXt V2 added GRN and global response normalization
Often matches or beats Swin Transformer with less compute
Faster inference than transformers — popular on edge

YOLOv8.explanation: Ultralytics YOLOv8 — state-of-the-art real-time object detection model
points: Anchor-free detection head
Mosaic augmentation + mixup training
Supports detection, segmentation, classification, pose estimation
Very fast on CPU and GPU
Active community and ecosystem (Ultralytics HUB)

Grounding DINO.explanation: Open-set object detection model that detects objects given text prompts
points: Combines DINO detector with grounded pre-training
Zero-shot detection — detects arbitrary objects via text
Excellent when combined with Segment Anything Model
Strong performance on COCO novel classes
Widely used in open-vocabulary pipelines

CLIP.explanation: Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining — foundation for vision-language understanding
points: Trained on 400 million image-text pairs
Zero-shot classification — matches text to image embeddings
Foundation for Stable Diffusion, DALL·E, Flamingo, LLaVA
OpenCLIP and OpenCLIP-ViT variants improve performance
Scaling laws still hold — bigger CLIP = better downstream performance

Stable Diffusion.explanation: Latent diffusion model that generates high-quality images from text
points: Latent diffusion — operates in lower-dimensional latent space
Stable Diffusion 1.5 → SDXL → SD3 → Flux.1 (2024–2025)
Open-source ecosystem — ControlNet, LoRA, IP-Adapter
Fine-tuning techniques: DreamBooth, Textual Inversion
Still dominant open-source image generation model in 2025

DINOv2.explanation: Self-supervised vision transformer that produces excellent feature representations
points: Self-distillation with no labels — knowledge distillation on large unlabeled data
Excellent frozen backbone for segmentation, detection, retrieval
DINOv2-g/14 is among the strongest open vision backbones
Registers (extra tokens) improve patch-level representations
Widely used in 2025 for vision foundation models
